three-column-preview-card-fm.setup: [ -d node_modules ] || if [ -f bun.lock ]; then b="${BUN:-$HOME/.bun/bin/bun}"; [ -x "$b" ] || b=$(command -v bun) || { echo 'setup: bun.lock but no bun (set BUN or install ~/.bun/bin/bun)' >&2; exit 1; }; NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG=/dev/null "$b" install --frozen-lockfile > /dev/null; else npm install --no-audit --no-fund > /dev/null 2>&1; fi
three-column-preview-card-fm._setup: Bun is this repo's package manager (Royer's pick, Oct 27, 2026, applied here Oct 28). A checkout with bun.lock installs with bun install --frozen-lockfile, bun found at $BUN, ~/.bun/bin/bun (not on PATH in non-interactive shells) or PATH. It ignores ~/.npmrc (NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG=/dev/null): Bun 1.4.4 refuses to install at all when that file holds a credential it can't parse, as Mac1's PPL Azure _password entry is (PR 252 QA, Oct 27, 2026), and this repo's packages all come from the public registry; a project .npmrc still applies. Its stderr stays in the stage log. An older branch without bun.lock keeps npm install. The checks call ./node_modules/.bin/<tool>, which either installer writes, and never pass --bun, so tsc, eslint and vitest keep running on Node through their #!/usr/bin/env node shebangs.

boat._setup: A boat box ships Bun 1.3.14, which can't read bun.lock, so it installs the packageManager's Bun first (a few seconds).
